text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax our request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- French President Jacques on Thursday made a pledge to the Hungarian Parliament that France would do its best to ensure that Hungary can join the European Union at the turn of the century. @

- The central budget dropped by HUF 100 billion last year or 3.3 percent of GDP, below the targeted 4 percent, and the current account deficit is expected to be $1.5-1.6 billion as against the planned $2 billion, government spokesman Elemer Kiss announced after the cabinet meeting.
- The Supreme Court yesterday passed a guilty verdict regarding the 1956 shooting of 46 protesters by security forces in Salgotarjan. @

- Democratic Forum president Sandor Lezsak and Christian Democrat president Gyorgy Giczy called for broad co-operation among opposition parties. Giczy said Hungary needs a moratorium of a few years on repaying state debt.
- The next round of Hungarian-Romanian foreign ministry talks will be held at deputy state secretary level in Bucharest on January 23-24.

- The black market accounts for 30 percent of the country's HUF 1,500 billion annual retail trade turnover, state secretary Jozsef Bencze said adding this means a HUF 200 billion loss to the central budget. @
- The BUX Index went up by over 200 points reaching 5,126.39 points, and the price of 13 shares rose to unseen heights in Thursday's trading.
-The Hungarian Development Bank announced the completion of its restructuring programme yesterday, spinning off several activities to both newly founded and existing subsidiaries.
- The textile manufacturer Grabotext Kft., a subsidiary of Graboplast, will spend HUF 500 million on modernising its equipment, said executive director Geza Szomolanyi. @
- The printing presses Kner and Petofi Nyomda will merge in six months, it was announced yesterday. Both companies belong to the French group Cofinec.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Representatives of ethnic Hungarian parties in Slovakia complained about the state of the Hungarian minority in their country in particular and the demotion of democratic principles in general when they met state secretary Csaba Tabajdi yesterday.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @

- Though Hungary may not yet be ready for the EU, it is no worse off in several areas than Union members, Andras Inotai, leader of the Workgroup for European Integration and president of the Budapest-based World Economy Institute, said yesterday.
- The traditionasl china manufacturer Herendi Porcelan has opened a retail outlet in the poshest district of Singapore.
- A 38,000-hectare area behind Budapest Nyugati railway sttion will be sold via an open auction on February 18, Gyorgy Magos, said vice president of the national railways MAV.
NAPI GAZDASAG @

- About 50 percent of the 5,000 workers at the Tiszai Eromu power plant will accept the generous severance package offered by the American owner AES Summit. The package was drawn up to circumvent a ban on dismissing workers contained in the privatisation contract.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The State Insurance Supervision has launched an investigation into insurance companies' practice of increasing life insurance premiums.
